current.text: Murray is a projected starter at forward. The projected starting five is Acuff, LaVine, Murray, Simmons and Sabonis.
He has not played in preseason and had ankle issues in camp.
Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan have left the Kings, which frees usage for Murray.
LaVine and Sabonis are still on the team and take many of the shots and touches, which limits his usage.
Experts expect more usage and big minutes, enough for about a top 100 season.
Experts doubt that his high block rate from last season will hold, especially with Ben Simmons in the starting lineup.
Draft him around pick 90. His upside is about 60th.
He is 26 and in the first year of a 5-year, 140 million USD contract. Coach Ham says this is the year he has to prove himself.
The Kings are one of the worst teams in the NBA. Their poor coaching, ownership and front office make the rotation hard to predict.
With a March 28 end, the Kings play 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks. That is 11 games. They have 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He has shot poorly from three every season since his rookie year. The shooting he showed as a rookie has not come back.
His usage rate has never reached 20.
Last season he missed most of the year. A finger injury hurt him early and an ankle injury hurt him late.
In a small sample last season he blocked many shots and defended well. Coach Ham says he has made big strides as a defender and rebounder.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: At Yahoo rank 100 and ESPN rank 83, Murray is a late pick in our 144-player draft. The markets price him at only 1.0 USD (Yahoo) and 1.7 USD (ESPN), and he went for 1 USD in our league last season, so he is a cheap end-of-auction buy with upside to about 60th. He fits every build because no category is weak, and he does not anchor any category either. Check three things early: his ankle (he missed preseason), whether his blocks hold next to Simmons, and whether his usage really goes up now that Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan are gone.
